{"id": "eb0f0402-9f67-4e7b-bba1-35c19ebac4e8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Launching an EC2 instance requires `ec2:RunInstances` as the core permission. But in practice, you'll typically need several additional permissions depending on what the instance launch involves, since `RunInstances` touches multiple resources:

- **`ec2:RunInstances`** — the core action to launch the instance
- **`iam:PassRole`** — if you're attaching an IAM instance profile/role to the instance
- **`ec2:CreateTags`** — if you want to tag the instance on creation
- **`ec2:CreateSecurityGroup`** / **`ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress`** — if a new security group is being created
- **`ec2:CreateVolume`** / **`ec2:AttachVolume`** — implicitly needed for EBS volumes attached at launch (covered under `RunInstances` but relevant if resource-level permissions are scoped)
- **`kms:CreateGrant`**, **`kms:Decrypt`**, **`kms:DescribeKey`** — if launching from an encrypted AMI/EBS snapshot

If you're scoping this with resource-level permissions or conditions (e.g., restricting by instance type, AMI, or VPC), the policy can get more granular — `RunInstances` supports many condition keys like `ec2:InstanceType`, `ec2:Region`, `ec2:Vpc`, etc.
